title: Bangladesh commits $130 million to eye care for 20 million people
excerpt: The five-year pledge, made at the first Global Summit for Eye Health, includes one million free cataract surgeries.
content:
Bangladesh has committed US$130 million over five years to strengthen eye care across the country, The Daily Star reported on 4 November. The pledge was made at the first Global Summit for Eye Health.

The commitment covers primary eye care for about 20 million people, one million free cataract surgeries and 10 million pairs of spectacles, according to the report.

The summit was hosted by Antigua and Barbuda and co-hosted by Bangladesh, Guyana, Ireland and Nigeria, with technical support from the World Health Organization (WHO). It was convened by the International Agency for the Prevention of Blindness (IAPB).

Who said what

Dr MA Muhit, state minister for health and family welfare, made the commitment on behalf of the government, the newspaper reported.

VisionSpring, a social enterprise, committed to providing eyeglasses to 7.5 million people in Bangladesh by 2030, according to Misha Mahjabeen, its managing director in Bangladesh.

The evidence

The article cites IAPB’s Value of Vision report, which estimates that about $129 million invested in eye health from 2026 to 2030 could bring about $2.31 billion in economic benefits. A national study found glaucoma in 3.2% of adults aged 35 and over. The THRIVE trial found that reading glasses for workers in near-vision jobs raised median monthly income by 33.4%.

Why it matters

Eye care NGOs and health partners will be needed to deliver screening and surgery at this scale. Organisations working with garment and transport workers may find new partnership openings.

What to watch

How the $130 million will be funded and delivered, and which partners the health ministry brings in.

Sources

  • Bangladesh commits $130m to expand eye care for 20 million people, The Daily Star, 4 November 2026
